results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 33 paragraph summaries match the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph (p01-p33) in spec order; the five introduction callouts are not spec paragraphs and are recorded with null. Volumes ¶2's two phrases are p13's two caveats.

Volumes Every Design Is Sized Against ¶2, the only unit marked two_ideas, holds one controlling idea: it opens 'Two caveats on reading it', which is p13's controlling idea ('Two caveats govern how to read the volumes'); both caveats serve it.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim: glance MV2/MV3, history MV3, brands MV2, volumes MV1/MV2, systems MV3, people MV1, problems MV4, program MV5, examples MV1/MV4, chapters MV1, introduction and conclusion the thesis as a whole.

Each table and figure is explained: glance table by p05, timeline by p07, brand table by p09-p10, Figure 1 by its caption beside p09, volumes table by p13's caveats, Figure 2 and the systems table by p14-p15, cast table by p16-p17, problems list and Figure 3 by p19, Figure 4 by p21, decision table by its lead-in and Figure 5's caption, worked-examples table by p26-p27, problem-to-chapter table by p29; p13's statistic is interpreted in the same paragraph.

Every boundary expresses its declared relationship: the glance follows the roadmap's first item; history 'That duplication comes from' (cause_effect); brands 'the four businesses that history assembled' (elaboration); p09 total (conclusion_summary); p11 'the exception' (contrast); p13 'Two caveats' (contrast); systems 'carries these volumes ... product of that history'; people 'have owners'; problems 'When Ingrid arrives' (time); program 'Veldmark's answer to these problems' (problem_solution); p21-p24 as declared; examples 'show the problems and the program's decisions' (example); p26 emphasis, p27 'the same role' (similarity), p28 'Smaller stories' (contrast); chapters, p30, p31 sequence and addition; conclusion 'one argument at three sizes' and p33 'So' (cause_effect).

Both flow readers describe the declared organising principle (what the group is, then its problems, then the program, then how the book uses it), each section's position is clear to both, and both find the page easy to follow overall. Failures below are individual lost-thread points.

results.quote: chairs the architecture advice forum (set up April 2027)
results.finding: The cast table names the architecture advice forum, 'the bikes split (new bike categories)' and 'the Listing event contract' before the page introduces them (in The Common Ground Program and its decision table); both readers lost the thread here. The spec's order is sound; the table's wording presumes later sections.
results.corroborated_by: flowB, item B1: 'People: Ingrid "chairs the architecture advice forum (set up April 2027)", Noor owns the roadmap "from the bikes split (new bike categories)" — neither introduced yet' (flowA item A3 reports the same).

results.corroborated_by: flowB, item B3: 'points to a figure after the table; table not visibly grouped into plateaus; could not match until the caption' (flowA item A5 reports the same).

The facts are in the spec; the prose does not say they are what the chapters show beyond the table row.

results.finding: Reader A could not reconcile problem 1's counts with the systems table, which has no product-catalog row and whose identity and trust-and-safety rows do not obviously total four. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: From the Preface to Part I ¶2
results.quote: and each chapter explains a decision about a boundary, not a product choice
results.finding: Reader B found the 'boundary' claim unprepared on this page. The spec's so-what asks for it and the previous preface page frames failures at boundaries; single reader.

Terms on does_not_know are either glossed where they first appear (VIN, DMS, DPE, KYB, AVM, DVF, GMV, DSA, p95, perceptual hash) or not used; liquidity and the failure-pattern names are on already_knows. The forward references to the advice forum, bikes split and Listing event contract are recorded once, under flow_is_followable.
The introduction opens with a direct statement of why the book uses one detailed fictional group and argues against both alternatives; no weak pattern.
The conclusion does not restate the sections, adds no new subtopic, and ends on a course of action and the hand-off to Part I.

'One argument at three sizes' ties the introduction, the failure patterns and Veldmark together, which no section states; the so-what (each chapter's scene is one more view of a known group; each chapter explains a decision about a boundary) and the takeaway (begin Part I as Ingrid began) are explicit.

The conclusion returns to the introduction's general-manager scene: the six minutes to searchable as problem 2 and the sold bike as Femke's €240 bike in 214 alert e-mails, as the spec's callback requires.

The cold reader predicted every roadmap promise in order: glance and history, brands and volumes, systems and people, the eight problems and Common Ground, the worked examples and how chapters use them, and a close tied back to the preface.

The reader named four problems with their patterns, all matching expected: Four of everything (Deal-Shaped Architecture), Six weeks for a category (The Category Straitjacket, The Attribute Junkyard), Duplicates at Hearthly (Seeing Double), Payment-link phishing (Fast Mail for Fraudsters), plus Overlap in Poland (Deal-Shaped Architecture).
The reader confirmed €225 and Monday 8 March, and corrected the buyer fee to €11.95 (5% of €225 plus €0.70) and the reservation to 14:02, exactly as expected.
